newsitem.title: UK: BP says refining margin could rise 50 cents.
newsitem.headline: BP says refining margin could rise 50 cents.

text.p: British Petroleum Plc said that its refining margins could improve by around 50 cents a barrel from the current level of around $2.00 a barrel if all its refineries were brought to the same level of efficiency.

In an interview with Reuters Financial Television's Inside Equities broadcast on Wednesday, BP chief executive John Browne said: "Not all our refineries are at the same level of efficiency yet. If we bring them all to the same level then we could potentially improve refining margins by about 50 cents a barrel. Right now the average refining margin is about $2.00 a barrel, so that is quite a big increase."
The company said on Tuesday that refining margins averaged $2.20 in 1996, but that they had been "very disappointing" in January. "Refining margins are tough," Browne told RFTV.

"There is overcapacity in the refining sector generally. We are trying to improve our refining margins in two ways, firstly by being selective in where we refine - we are closing down or selling some of our refineries - and secondly by operating each of them to the highest possible level of efficiency."
Browne was also upbeat about potential cost savings from the merger of its downstream operations with those of Mobil Corp.

"I think we will see some benefits coming through this year," he said, adding: "We expect to save and have synergy benefits of at least $500 million per year - and I think that number is rising the whole time - by the end of the third year of the merger."
